chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele more at the 8q24 enhancer and lowers POU5F1B to modulate CRC risk

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele if the HMG/Sox family model reflects TCF7L2. TCF7L2 has ENCODE ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in HCT116 and is well expressed there (E05). However, TCF7L2 has no own QBiC-SELEX model; E35 uses CIS-BP-mapped LEF1/TCF7/TCF7L1 models, with best effect -0.47 (ref > alt; z -4.66) and a strong site. I therefore treat the allelic direction as family-level and weak, not as a TCF7L2 own-model measurement.

rs6983267 lies in the active proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447, and TCF7L2 has a ChIP-seq peak over this region in HCT116. E03 z-scores are maxima across biosamples, so HCT116-specific enhancer activity is not directly proven.

The element is linked to POU5F1B by L2G (best gene score 0.89) and by a colon transverse eQTL in which alt T is associated with higher POU5F1B (NES +0.20). POU5F1B is a literature-supported colorectal cancer oncogene. This chain requires TCF7L2 to repress POU5F1B so that lower TCF7L2 binding on T fits higher POU5F1B on T; that repression is an assumption, not shown by perturbation or reporter evidence. L2G is also dominated by prostate/PSA credible sets, not CRC-specific credible sets.

The relevant context is colorectal: HCT116 is the matching ENCODE/DepMap colorectal carcinoma line with TCF7L2 expression and occupancy, and GTEx colon transverse shows the POU5F1B eQTL. HCT116 is a carcinoma line, not normal colon.

The strongest CRC GWAS endpoint lists the alt T allele as the effect allele. If T reduces TCF7L2 occupancy and TCF7L2 represses POU5F1B, T would raise POU5F1B and increase CRC risk. E15 also contains CRC/colon endpoints with G as the effect allele, so the disease-allele direction is not fully consistent across studies.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP or footprinting will show stronger TCF7L2 occupancy on ref G than alt T in colorectal cells.
TCF7L2 knockdown or CRISPR perturbation should change POU5F1B expression in a direction consistent with TCF7L2 repressing POU5F1B at this element.
Editing G>T in HCT116 should alter POU5F1B expression and enhancer activity in a TCF7L2-dependent manner.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 ChIP or footprinting is not allele-specific at this base.
TCF7L2 perturbation does not affect POU5F1B expression in colorectal cells.
The CRC association is fully explained by another variant in LD that changes a different TF or element.

chains.title: NR2F2 binds the alt T allele more and activates POU5F1B in colorectal cells

links.claim: NR2F2 is predicted to bind the alt T allele more strongly by QBiC-SELEX: effect +1.92 (alt > ref; z 20.82), with a strong site. However, the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped NR2F6 model, not clearly an NR2F2 own model, and the same QBiC model/effect appears for NR1D1/NR1D2 in E33/E34, so NR2F2 specificity is weak. E36 reports no NR2F2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT116; the only reported peak is in HepG2/liver. Occupancy in the matching colorectal cell line is therefore missing.

The variant is in the active pELS EH38E3858447, but the claim that this is an NR2F2-responsive enhancer rests on a CIS-BP-mapped NR2F6 model and is not validated by NR2F2 occupancy in colorectal cells. E36 provides no HCT116 NR2F2 peak over the variant.

The element is linked to POU5F1B by L2G and by a colon transverse eQTL where alt T increases POU5F1B. This chain assumes NR2F2 activates POU5F1B, so stronger NR2F2 binding on T would fit the eQTL direction. That activation step is not supported by perturbation or reporter evidence.
NR2F2 is expressed in HCT116, and the eQTL is in colon transverse, but direct NR2F2 occupancy in colorectal cells is not established by the given evidence; E36 reports only HepG2 occupancy.

If alt T increases NR2F2 binding and NR2F2 activates POU5F1B, T would increase POU5F1B and promote colorectal cancer. The chain is limited because NR2F2 occupancy at this base in HCT116 is not shown and the NR2F2 motif specificity is weak.

predictions: NR2F2 should occupy this element in colorectal cells, with stronger binding on alt T than ref G.
NR2F2 perturbation should change POU5F1B expression in the direction expected for an activator.
The effect should be absent in cells that do not express NR2F2.
falsified_if: NR2F2 does not occupy this element in colorectal cells.
NR2F2 binding is not allele-specific at this base.
NR2F2 perturbation does not affect POU5F1B expression.

chains.title: SRF binds the ref G allele more at the same enhancer and represses POU5F1B

links.claim: SRF binds the ref G allele more strongly than alt T in its own QBiC-SELEX model: effect -1.191 (ref > alt; z -7.74), and SRF has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT116 and is expressed there. However, E21 reports the best SRF site is weak on both alleles (ref 95.1st, alt 91.3rd percentile; neither reaches 97.5th), so the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element. Allele-specific SRF occupancy is not shown.
The variant lies in the active pELS EH38E3858447, and SRF has a ChIP-seq peak over this region in HCT116. This supports element localization, not allele-specific SRF function.

The element is linked to POU5F1B by L2G and by a colon transverse eQTL in which alt T increases POU5F1B. This chain assumes that SRF represses POU5F1B, so lower SRF binding on T would fit higher POU5F1B on T. The SRF-repression step is not supported by perturbation or reporter evidence.
SRF is expressed and bound in HCT116, and the eQTL context is colon transverse, making a colorectal cell context plausible. This does not establish allele-specific SRF function.

If alt T lowers SRF occupancy and SRF represses POU5F1B, T would increase POU5F1B and could contribute to CRC risk. The phenotype link is weak because the SRF motif is weak on both alleles and no SRF-specific CRC or POU5F1B perturbation evidence is provided.

predictions: Allele-specific SRF ChIP should show stronger SRF occupancy on ref G than alt T in HCT116 or colon cells.
SRF knockdown should change POU5F1B expression if SRF acts through this element.
The SRF effect should be weaker than TCF7L2 because the SRF site is weak on both alleles by QBiC-SELEX.
falsified_if: SRF does not occupy the variant base by allele-specific ChIP or footprinting.
SRF perturbation does not alter POU5F1B expression.
The SRF ChIP peak is explained entirely by a nearby site rather than the variant.

grades_v0.reason: ENCODE ChIP-seq supports TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant in HCT116 (E05), but occupancy is not allele-specific. The QBiC-SELEX change is not from a TCF7L2 own model: E20 uses a CIS-BP-mapped LEF1 model, and the claim itself says the QBiC direction is family-level. Thus the allele-specific direction for TCF7L2 is supported only by a surrogate model.

E03 places the variant in pELS EH38E3858447 with DNase/H3K27ac cCRE annotation, and E05 reports a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT116. Caveat: E03 z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not HCT116-specific.

The variant-to-POU5F1B link is supported by L2G and by a colon transverse eQTL (E16, E17), and POU5F1B has CRC literature support (E18b-d). However, the claim that TCF7L2 occupancy represses POU5F1B is an assumption, not shown by perturbation or reporter evidence.

E05 supports TCF7L2 expression and occupancy in HCT116, and E17 provides a colon transverse eQTL for POU5F1B. The context is colorectal-relevant, although HCT116 is a carcinoma line and not normal colon.

E15 gives a very strong CRC GWAS association with effect allele T, and E18c-d support POU5F1B as oncogenic. But the TCF7L2-specific step is inferential, and E15 itself contains CRC/colon endpoints with G as the effect allele, so allele-to-phenotype direction is not fully consistent.

SRF has an HCT116 ChIP-seq peak over the variant and an own-model QBiC-SELEX effect in the ref>alt direction (E09, E21), but the best SRF site is weak on both alleles and the ChIP peak may reflect another site in the element. Allele-specific SRF occupancy is not shown.
E03 supports the active pELS annotation and E09 supports an SRF ChIP-seq peak over this region in HCT116. This supports element localization, not allele-specific function.

The variant-to-POU5F1B link is supported by L2G/eQTL evidence, but the SRF-specific claim that SRF represses POU5F1B is not supported by any perturbation or reporter evidence. The gene link is shared and not SRF-specific.
E09 shows SRF expression and an HCT116 ChIP peak, and E17 provides a colon transverse eQTL context. This is adequate for cell-type plausibility, though not for allele-specific SRF function.
The phenotype claim depends on an unproven SRF-repression model and a weak SRF motif. E15 and E18c-d provide CRC/POU5F1B context, but no SRF-specific phenotype evidence.

QBiC-SELEX gives a strong alt>ref effect, but E29 reports the best model as a CIS-BP-mapped NR2F6 model, and the same QBiC line appears for NR1D1/NR1D2 in E33/E34. This is not clearly NR2F2-specific. Occupancy over the variant is reported only in HepG2/liver, not HCT116, so relevant-cell-type occupancy is missing.

E03 supports the active pELS annotation, but the claim that it is an NR2F2-responsive enhancer rests on the QBiC motif, which is an NR2F6-mapped model and not validated NR2F2 occupancy in colorectal cells.

The variant-to-POU5F1B eQTL/L2G link is supported, but the claim that NR2F2 activates POU5F1B is not supported by perturbation or reporter evidence. Direction is consistent only under an unproven activation assumption.
NR2F2 is expressed in HCT116 and there is a colon transverse eQTL, but direct NR2F2 occupancy in colorectal cells is not established. The claim itself acknowledges this gap.
The phenotype link is an inference from an unproven NR2F2 activation effect plus CRC/POU5F1B literature. No NR2F2-specific CRC or POU5F1B perturbation evidence is cited.
